text:
Your own home screen and phone remote for the TV. 
 Scenes with a glass clock, your apps in your order, Keep watching across apps,
 and a phone remote that finds a show and starts it. No ads on the home screen. Open source.
 

 
 
 
 
 

 
 Set it up 
  ·  Which TVs 
  ·  Docs 
  ·  What's new 
 

 Get started

First time? docs/START-HERE.md walks you through it, one step at a time.

1. With the TV remote, the easiest way. On Google TV and Android TV you need no computer: the
 steps for your TV are at couchtv.joshuaseage.com/get,
 with the free Setup app for the TVs that need a Mac or Windows computer once (Fire TV, or the Home
 button on Google TV from a computer). It also checks whether your TV will work.
2. With your AI agent. Open this folder in Claude Code (it needs a paid Claude plan; any coding AI
 agent works) and say "set this up on my TV". It reads AGENTS.md, finds your TV, asks
 which option you want and a few questions (who watches, the look, your apps), reads the plan back,
 and changes nothing on the TV until you say yes.
3. By hand: docs/SETUP.md has every step, from developer mode to the TV home,
 and how to undo it.

 Pick the way for your TV before you start. Not every way does the whole job on every TV:

 Way What you need Google TV Android TV Fire TV Samsung or LG 
 --- --- --- --- --- --- 
 AI agent (AGENTS.md) A computer on the TV's Wi-Fi with Claude Code (a paid Claude plan) or another coding agent Yes, Home button included Yes Yes, Home button included (Amazon's home flashes up first). The full phone remote keeps a computer on at home Yes, as an app that a computer at home that stays on opens. Their own Home button still opens their own menu 
 From your phone (website) The TV remote and a phone on the same Wi-Fi. No computer Yes. From 0.13.9, Let the phone press keys, then one press of Make Home open Couch TV, gives it the Home button with no computer (not yet tried on a real Google TV; the Setup app still does it from a computer) Yes. On Android TV 10 and newer the app asks Android to make it the home Only part: Home needs three one off grants from a computer, and on current Fire OS the phone remote can't press keys or type No 
 Setup app (website) A Mac or Windows computer on the same Wi-Fi, once Yes, Home button included Yes, Android TV 7.1 and newer Yes on Fire OS 6, 7 and 8 (Amazon's home flashes up first) No 
 By hand (docs/SETUP.md) A Mac or Linux computer with Python 3.11 or newer Yes Yes on-tv/README.md, Fire TV docs/SAMSUNG.md, docs/LG.md, with a computer at home that stays on 

Other TVs: Will it work on my TV?

 [!NOTE]
 Set couch-tv up with 0.10 or older on a Google TV? 0.11 and newer leave the Google home and setup
 apps switched on. Read If your TV loops after a restart
 before you next restart your TV.

 

 Updates

The newest release is 0.13.15 , on the Releases page: a redesigned Couch TV Setup that links your TV to your account after asking whose it is, an optional Tidy up your TV step, and a Make it yours card on a new TV (details). 0.13.14 brought: Couch TV Setup can stay on your computer as Couch TV Helper for extras like turning the TV on from your phone, and Couch TV Studio can show the apps on your TV (details). 0.13.13 brought: your names, photos, town and guest Wi-Fi can come from your Couch TV account, Couch TV Setup finds the TV on your Wi-Fi and links it to your account so a design you send goes on with one click, and widgets get Glass and Liquid glass text (details). 0.13.12 made getting a design by code tell Couch TV Studio the TV has Couch TV, and the Now playing card follow Spotify at once and send nothing to Spotify (details). 0.13.11 made one Add apps sheet fill a folder, the Dock, an app grid or Games with every app on the TV, widgets in Jost or Cormorant Garamond draw in those fonts, and the on-TV app moved to its own signing key (details). 0.13.10 made the on-TV app set up in two steps, a new TV opens on a one question welcome, and widgets that need your town, calendar or photos are set up on your phone (details). 0.13.9 made the on-TV app update itself with one button, Home settings can be changed from your phone or a computer, a phone pairs in one scan, a couch-tv Studio design can be sent from the phone instead of typed with the remote, each widget has its own settings, and settings and setup use plain words (details). 0.13.8 made Home settings pages such as Update couch-tv open at the top, with Up reaching the lines above the first button (details). 0.13.7 made sure Hold OK never opens the app on a TCL either, the arrow that points at the Settings gear reaches it, and on a Samsung Home settings, About shows the version and how to update, while a Frame opens couch-tv more reliably after Art Mode (details). 0.13.6 brought update news on the TV (Home settings, About, Update couch-tv, now on the on-TV app too), a Settings gear that never covers a widget, and a Hold OK that never opens the app (details). 0.13.5 brought fixes from a real beginner on a TCL (Use as home screen asks properly and Cancel means no, the TV says plainly when Google keeps the Home button, and design codes are easy to type with the remote) (details). 0.13.4 brought Samsung, with couch-tv Studio, a setup you run yourself with no AI agent ( couch-tv-samsung-setup.zip ), and a Frame that opens couch-tv after Art Mode and goes to Art Mode when the phone says off; plus couch-tv Studio designs in the Apple TV app (details). 0.13.3 made it easier for beginners (a Settings button on every design, a phone only install that no longer asks for the accessibility permission Play Protect flags, plain words on the TV and in the Setup app), greeted guests by name with no computer, and brought your home into couch-tv Studio. 0.13.2 brought Ask AI, your own AI agent, smart home set up on the TV and designs on Roku. New in 0.13:

- 14 November: custom cards with a web link open in the TV's browser on Android TV, LG and Samsung, thanks ekagra-c
